prompt:
You are a graphics engineer's vision analyst. These 8 frames are consecutive samples (in order, frame 1 -> frame 8) from a tilt-demonstration segment of the YouTube video "All 39 Pokemon Card Holo Patterns Explained" by Sleeve No Card Behind. This segment covers the holofoil pattern the creator calls "Diagonal sheen (right)". A person tilts a real card (or raw foil sheet) under a single light source so the foil animates. Frame timestamps (seconds into video): 912.7s, 913.6s, 914.5s, 915.4s, 916.3s, 917.2s, 918.1s, 919.0s.

Creator's narration for this segment (auto-transcript, may have small errors):
---
rotated to now be diagonal. There are a handful of these secret variants out there, and they aren't too hard to find, but I do feel like a cracked ice or cosmos variant would have been way more exciting. After these rolled out, this diagonal pattern was adopted as the default holo pattern for the next [music] few sets. But it doesn't end there. The exact same pattern exists,
---

Produce an implementation-grade spec of this foil pattern for a ShaderMaterial author who cannot watch the video. Use EXACTLY these markdown sections:

## Cards Shown
Identify every distinct physical card visible across the frames: card name printed on it, and your best set/era guess. If a raw uncut foil sheet is shown instead, say so. Cite the frames each appears in.

## Static Appearance
What the foil looks like in a single frame: element shapes (stars, orbs, lines, cells...), their approximate scale relative to card width, observed colors, and WHERE on the card the foil lives (background behind subject / full face / border / art window only).

## Tilt Animation
The heart of the spec. Describe what CHANGES between frames as the card tilts: what moves and in which direction, whether color travels across elements (hue rotation) or elements brighten/dim in place, whether sparkles pop in/out abruptly or breathe smoothly, any parallax (layers moving against each other), and the apparent speed/scale of the change per degree of tilt. Tie every claim to specific frame pairs (e.g. "between frame 3 and frame 5 ...").

## Layer Structure Hypothesis
Your best guess at the physical construction: how many visual layers, what each contributes, what is foil vs printed ink, whether the pattern is in the foil embossing or printed on top.

## Distinguishing Features
How to tell this pattern apart from similar ones (e.g. star-based vs orb-based, sheen band vs full-field, glitter vs dots). Name lookalikes if you know them.

## Shader Notes
Concrete recipe hints: what a fragment shader needs (cell noise / stripe function / sheen band / glitter hash...), what the tilt uniform should drive, hue ramp behavior, and any parallax offsets. 5-10 bullet points.

## Confidence
Per section above, High/Medium/Low with a one-line justification. Anything you could NOT verify in the frames must be Low.

Hard rules: describe only what is visible in the frames or stated in the narration; never invent card names you cannot read; if frames show a talking head or unrelated b-roll, say which frames those are and exclude them from analysis.
